result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [get_adam_dataset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: Get the template for a type of ADaM dataset. twitter-card: title: >- [get_adam_dataset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: Get the template for a type of ADaM dataset. title: >- [get_adam_dataset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get the template for a type of ADaM dataset. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the template for a type of ADaM dataset. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_adam_templates.py#L925-L995){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature get_adam_dataset(name) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Pointblank has templates for four types of CDISC Analysis Data Model (ADaM) dataset: ADSL (the subject-level analysis dataset), BDS (the Basic Data Structure, used by datasets such as ADVS and ADLB), ADAE (adverse events) and ADTTE (time to event). Each template is an [`ADaMDatasetTemplate`](`pointblank.ADaMDatasetTemplate`): the dataset's label and class, the variables that form its natural key, and an [`ADaMVariableSpec`](`pointblank.ADaMVariableSpec`) for each of its variables. The templates are what [`validate_adam()`](`pointblank.validate_adam`), [`validate_adam_structure()`](`pointblank.validate_adam_structure`) and [`adam_to_metadata()`](`pointblank.adam_to_metadata`) work from. The templates cover the common variables of each type of dataset rather than every variable that the ADaM Implementation Guide describes. Each call returns a new template object, so changing one doesn't affect later calls. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The template name: `"ADSL"`, `"BDS"`, `"ADAE"` or `"ADTTE"`. This is case-insensitive. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ADaMDatasetTemplate]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The template for the dataset. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If there is no template with that name. The error message lists the templates, as does [`list_adam_datasets()`](`pointblank.list_adam_datasets`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's get the template for the subject-level analysis dataset: ::: {#ac3b2e7d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb adsl = pb.get_adam_dataset("adsl") print(adsl.label) print(adsl.natural_keys) print(adsl.required_variables) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Subject Level Analysis Dataset ['STUDYID', 'USUBJID'] ['STUDYID', 'USUBJID', 'SUBJID', 'SITEID', 'TRT01P'] ``` ::: ::: ADSL has one record per subject, so the study and subject identifiers are its natural key. Besides the identifiers, the planned treatment `TRT01P` is required. The template also lists the population flags: ::: {#a402a192 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} adsl.population_flags ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['SAFFL', 'ITTFL', 'EFFFL', 'RANDFL', 'ENRLFL', 'PPROTFL', 'COMPLFL'] ``` ::: ::: These flags (safety, intent-to-treat, efficacy and so on) are conditionally required or permissible, and [`validate_adam()`](`pointblank.validate_adam`) checks that the ones in a dataset hold only `"Y"` and `"N"`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~list_adam_datasets`) : List the dataset templates. [](`~ADaMDatasetTemplate`) : The template that is returned. [](`~validate_adam`) : Build a validation plan from an ADaM dataset template. [](`~get_sdtm_domain`) : The equivalent for SDTM domains.
